rationale.consistency: Uses Copy()/RepoDir scoping, cmdutil.FlagErrorf, MutuallyExclusive, heredoc help and the WorktreeRemove style for WorktreeAdd; fits surrounding packages well.
rationale.edge_cases: Blank path, missing --checkout, --list exclusivity, relative->abs, branch-repo remote selection, reuse-existing-worktree, symlink/non-dir guard and ff-only pull warning all covered; no worktree success hint unlike pr checkout.
rationale.scope: Beyond the asked move of path rules to shared, it also relocates worktreeCheckoutCmds into shared, swaps localBranchExists (show-ref) for HasLocalBranch, and changes pr checkout to use abs paths in -C and messages; unrequested behaviour shifts.
rationale.readability: checkoutWorktree is short and clear; WorktreeCheckoutCommands returns a [][]string that is documented to always hold one command, an awkward shape; help text sentence is slightly ungrammatical.
rationale.robustness: Errors propagated, pull failure downgraded to a warning as in the existing flow, nil baseRemote handled by the pre-existing early return; no panics or resource issues.
rationale.maintainability: Two parallel implementations of the same git worktree commands now exist (git.WorktreeAdd used by develop, shared.WorktreeCheckoutCommands used by pr checkout), so a future change must be made twice; WorktreeAdd's empty-remoteBranch mode switch is a magic-parameter API.
